text:
**Short answer:** for a typical full-size fridge, get a power station with about 1,000 Wh for most of a day, or 1,500-2,000 Wh for a full 24 hours or more. It should also have a surge rating of at least 1,300 W and a pure sine wave inverter.

**How the numbers work**
- **Running watts:** a full-size fridge draws about 100-250 W while the compressor runs, which almost any 1,000 W-class station can handle ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
- **Startup surge:** the compressor briefly spikes to roughly 900-2,400 W. A station with plenty of battery can still fail if its inverter can't cover this ([HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)).
- **Energy per day:** the compressor only runs about a third of the time. An ENERGY STAR 18 cu ft fridge averages about 41 W, or roughly 1,400 Wh per 24 hours once you allow for inverter losses and 20% headroom ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator)).
- **Your own fridge:** check the yellow EnergyGuide label. Average watts = kWh/year × 1,000 ÷ 8,760. A large side-by-side with an ice maker can use about twice the typical figure.

**Options by outage length** (runtimes are HomeGrid HQ's estimates for a typical fridge)
- **Under a day (~1,000 Wh):**
  - Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 has 1,070 Wh, about 17 hours, and costs $449-799 recently.
  - BLUETTI AC180 has 1,152 Wh and 1,800 W (2,700 W peak), and costs $399-699 recently ([BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)).
- **About a day or more (~2,000 Wh):**
  - Anker SOLIX S2000 is listed at $699.99 after coupon ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator)).
  - EcoFlow Delta 3 Max (2,048 Wh, about 33 hours, $879) and Jackery Explorer 2000 v2 (2,042 Wh, about 33 hours, $899) are also in this range ([HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)).
- **Multi-day outages (3,000 Wh+):** the Bluetti Elite 300 (3,014 Wh) runs about 2 days, at $1,199 ([HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/)).

**Tips:** keep the door closed (food is unsafe after about 4 hours above 40°F). Add the wattage of anything else you plan to run, and test your fridge on the station before an outage.

I didn't give a purchase link for each model because the search results only had review and guide pages, not direct store links. The sources above list current prices and "check price" buttons.
